title: Upper Sixth ICT — First Term Learning Notes
source_note: The supplied file is named Upper Sixth but its printed heading says LOWERSIXTH. Its lesson sequence is used as supplied; the discrepancy is not silently treated as an official correction.
objectives_note: Objectives transcribed from the supplied progression, with punctuation and capitalisation normalised. Integration lessons have no objectives printed in the sheet; their tasks and criteria are locally authored.

parts.title: Using the Internet to communicate and collaborate

lessons.title: The Concept of Artificial Intelligence
objectives: Define AI and explain its history and development.
Identify and describe the main types of AI.
Explain common application areas of AI.

lessons.title: AI Ethics and Responsible Use
objectives: Explain ethical issues associated with AI.
Examine the potential risks and benefits of AI.
Discuss principles for the responsible use of AI.

lessons.title: AI Techniques and Intelligent Systems
objectives: Describe common AI techniques and their applications.
Explain the characteristics of intelligent systems (smart school, smart city, smart health, smart home).
Compare AI techniques and intelligent systems based on their applications.

lessons.title: Machine Learning
objectives: Define Machine Learning (ML) and explain its relationship with AI.
Explain the basic principles of Machine Learning.
Build and test simple Machine Learning models using Teachable Machine.

lessons.title: Developing AI Systems
objectives: Describe the major stages involved in developing an AI system.
Identify programming languages and tools used in AI development.
Explain why Python is widely used in AI development.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Applying AI to Improve Living and Working Standards
Fundamentals of Computer Networks
objectives: Describe a computer network.
Compare networked computers with stand-alone systems.
Identify real-world examples of computer networks (e.g., home Wi-Fi, school labs, the internet) versus standalone computer setups.

lessons.title: Network Complexity and Operational Challenges
objectives: Identify and discuss the benefits and limitations of networks.
Explain the complexity involved in setting up and maintaining data communication networks.
Explain the complexity of interoperability between heterogeneous systems.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Networking a Real Organisation: Description and Challenges
Types of Networks by Coverage Area
objectives: Describe types of networks (LAN, MAN, WAN, CAN, PAN).
Classify properly based on coverage a given network (e.g., home Wi-Fi setup, a university).
Compare the network types in terms of coverage area, typical speed, cost, and number of devices/users supported.

lessons.title: Choosing the Right Network for an Organisation
objectives: Identify the networking needs of different types of organizations.
Select the most appropriate network type for a given organizational scenario.
Evaluate the key factors involved in choosing one network type over another for a specific organization's needs.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Classifying and Choosing Networks for Organisations
Network Architecture (Peer-to-Peer and Client/Server)
objectives: Explain network types based on the logical relationship between nodes.
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each configuration.
Choose the appropriate network design for a given organisation.

lessons.title: Types of Physical Network Topologies
objectives: Describe the types of physical network topologies (mesh, star, ring, bus, tree).
Identify the physical layout and connection pattern of each topology.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of each topology.

lessons.title: Comparing and Choosing Network Topologies
objectives: Compare the different types of physical network topologies.
Evaluate which topology suits specific organisational needs.
Propose a suitable network topology for a given organisation.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Designing the Architecture and Topology of an Organisation's Network
Network Equipment
objectives: Explain the role of key network components (modem, hub, router, NOS…).
Differentiate between the various network components based on their functions.
Identify the appropriate network components required for a computer network.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Computer Network
objectives: Demonstrate the steps involved in setting up a basic computer network.
Identify the essential equipment and how they are interconnected.
Set up and test a peer-to-peer computer network.

lessons.title: Selecting Equipment for Organisational Networks
objectives: Select appropriate network equipment for specific organizational needs (e.g., a school).
Explain the factors to consider when selecting network components.
Plan and design a network setup suitable for an organization's size and purpose.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — From Design to a Working Network
Intranet and Extranet
objectives: Explain the concept of an intranet and an extranet.
Explain the technologies and requirements used to implement intranets and extranets.
Contrast the uses of intranets and extranets in organisations.

lessons.title: Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) and Privacy
objectives: Describe the principles of a Virtual Private Network (VPN).
Explain how protocols are used to ensure privacy and confidentiality during data transmission.
Set up a secured VPN using firewalls and digital signatures.

lessons.title: Computer and Network Security
objectives: Explain concepts related to computer and data security (confidentiality, integrity, availability).
Identify security measures used to protect computer systems (including user accounts, passwords, authentication, firewalls and security protocols).
Explain how digital signatures, encryption and other security measures help protect computer systems.

lessons.title: Data Protection and Access Control
objectives: Explain how encryption and access rights are used to protect computer data.
Describe methods used to control access to data and prevent unauthorised use.
Explain the importance of protecting data confidentiality, integrity and availability.

lessons.title: Data Validation and Verification Techniques
objectives: Explain and contrast the concepts of data validation and verification.
Describe validation techniques (e.g., range check, format check, length check…).
Describe verification techniques such as visual check and double entry.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Securing an Organisation's Networked Information System
Modes of Data Transmission
objectives: Explain logical topology methods (CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA).
Describe different transmission modes (simplex, half-duplex, full duplex).
Illustrate the direction of signal flow for a given data transmission scenario.

lessons.title: Broadband and Narrowband Transmission
objectives: Define broadband and narrowband transmission.
Differentiate between broadband and narrowband transmissions.
Identify the appropriate transmission type used in a given communication situation.

lessons.title: Types of Data Transmission
objectives: Explain and contrast serial and parallel data transmission methods.
Differentiate between synchronous and asynchronous transmission and identify their use in given situations.
Illustrate and differentiate between analog and digital signals.

lessons.title: Transmission Media (Guided and Unguided)
objectives: Describe guided (wired) transmission media (e.g., copper wire, coaxial cable, optical fibre…).
Describe unguided (wireless) transmission media (e.g., Bluetooth, microwave, Wi-Fi…).
Choose an appropriate transmission medium for a given context.

lessons.title: Peripheral Device Control Mechanisms
objectives: Explain the meaning and role of buffers, interrupts, interrupt priorities, polling and handshaking in controlling peripheral devices.
Differentiate between the various techniques used to control communication between the computer and peripheral devices.
Determine the technique used to control a device in a given network scenario.

lessons.title: Network Protocols and Their Roles in Data Transmission
objectives: Explain the meaning and role of network protocols in data transmission.
Discuss the functions of protocols (e.g., IP, TCP, HTTP…) in communication.
Evaluate how TCP/IP and other protocols facilitate reliable and efficient data transmission.

lessons.title: Protocol Suites and the OSI Reference Model
objectives: Explain the role of protocol suites in network communication.
Describe the seven layers of the OSI reference model and their functions.
Relate network protocols to the appropriate layers of the OSI reference model.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Analysing and Optimising Data Transmission for an Organisation
Error Detection and Data Transfer Checks
objectives: Identify errors that may occur during data transmission.
Describe data transfer checking mechanisms used to detect transmission errors.
Explain parity checks as methods of error detection.

lessons.title: History and Development of the Internet
objectives: Define the Internet and explain its purpose.
Recall major events in the history of the Internet.
Explain factors that led to growth of the internet.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of the internet.

lessons.title: Internet Connectivity Technologies and Requirements
objectives: Identify the technologies used to connect computers and networks to the Internet.
Describe the role of devices in providing Internet connectivity.
Use core features of a browser.

lessons.title: Social Networks and Collaborative Environments
objectives: Define and identify examples of social media and collaborative environments.
Describe the positive and negative impacts of social networks and Internet use in the community.
Propose measures for the responsible and proper use of social media.
Demonstrate how collaborative platforms can be used for communication, learning and teamwork.

lessons.title: Internet Services and Information Retrieval
objectives: Describe the major services provided through the Internet.
Create an e-mail account, attach a file to an e-mail and send it.
Research information on a particular topic using retrieval services.

lessons.title: Internet Communication and Teleworking
objectives: Explain the concepts of teleworking, telecommuting and videoconferencing.
Explain the use of URLs and cookies when accessing web services.
Set up and use a teleconferencing platform for online communication.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Connecting, Collaborating and Communicating Online
Electronic Services: E-commerce, E-health and E-government
objectives: Define some major electronic services (e-commerce, e-health and e-government).
Describe some major electronic services.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of using electronic services.

lessons.title: Applications, Benefits and Challenges of Electronic Services
objectives: Compare the applications of e-commerce, e-health and e-government in everyday life.
Identify e-government platforms and explain their advantages and limits.
Identify appropriate electronic services for solving common problems in the community.

lessons.title: Computer-Assisted Learning (CAL) and E-learning
objectives: Describe Computer-Assisted Learning (CAL) and its role in the learning process.
Identify different methods of course delivery (e.g., delivery through servers, CD-ROMs, e-books).
Explain the advantages and limitations of CAL and e-learning.

lessons.title: Integration Activities — Designing a Digital Services and Learning Programme
Developing Simple Web Pages Using HTML
objectives: Identify the role of tags and attributes in a web page.
Implement basic HTML tags to structure a web page.
Create simple web pages using HTML and a text editor.
